title: Correct refractive index
description: Essential: The final answer for part (1) must be √3 or its decimal equivalent (approximately 1.732).

title: Correct speed of light
description: Essential: The final answer for part (2) must be c/√3 or its equivalent (e.g., √3c/3, 0.577c).

title: Angle identification
description: Important: The solution must correctly identify the angle of incidence on face AB as 60° and the angle of refraction as 30°, using geometry of the equilateral triangle and the given beam directions.

title: Application of Snell's Law
description: Important: The solution must explicitly apply Snell's law (n = sin(i)/sin(r)) using the identified angles to find the refractive index.

title: Speed-index relationship
description: Important: The solution must correctly use the relationship v = c / n to find the speed in the medium from the refractive index.

title: Geometry justification
description: Optional: The solution includes a clear diagram or step-by-step geometric reasoning to justify the 60° and 30° angles.

title: Unit consistency
description: Optional: The solution for speed maintains correct units (e.g., m/s) or explicitly states speed as a fraction of c.

title: Angle confusion error
description: Pitfall: Incorrectly identifying the angles of incidence or refraction (e.g., using 30° and 60° in the wrong order in Snell's law).

title: Incorrect formula application
description: Pitfall: Using an incorrect formula for refractive index (e.g., n = sin(r)/sin(i)) or for speed (e.g., v = n*c).
